items.abstract:
<jats:p>
            Effective fuzzing of programs that process structured binary inputs, such as multimedia files, is a challenging task, since those programs expect a very specific input format. Existing fuzzers, however, are mostly
            <jats:italic>format-agnostic,</jats:italic>
            which makes them versatile, but also ineffective when a specific format is required.
          </jats:p>
          <jats:p>
            We present
            <jats:sc>FormatFuzzer</jats:sc>
            , a generator for
            <jats:italic>format-specific fuzzers</jats:italic>
            .
            <jats:sc>FormatFuzzer</jats:sc>
            takes as input a
            <jats:italic>binary template</jats:italic>
            (a format specification used by the 010 Editor) and compiles it into C++ code that acts as
            <jats:italic>parser,</jats:italic>
            <jats:italic>mutator,</jats:italic>
            and highly efficient
            <jats:italic>generator</jats:italic>
            of inputs conforming to the rules of the language.
          </jats:p>
          <jats:p>
            The resulting format-specific fuzzer can be used as a standalone producer or mutator in black-box settings, where no guidance from the program is available. In addition, by providing mutable
            <jats:italic>decision seeds,</jats:italic>
            it can be easily
            <jats:italic>integrated</jats:italic>
            with arbitrary
            <jats:italic>format-agnostic fuzzers</jats:italic>
            such as AFL to make them format-aware. In our evaluation on complex formats such as MP4 or ZIP,
            <jats:sc>FormatFuzzer</jats:sc>
            showed to be a highly effective producer of valid inputs that also detected previously unknown memory errors in
            <jats:monospace>ffmpeg</jats:monospace>
            and
            <jats:monospace>timidity</jats:monospace>
            .
          </jats:p>
title:
<scp>FormatFuzzer</scp>
            : Effective Fuzzing of Binary File Formats
